business.body:
- Three-segment structure: CDMO (Piramal Pharma Solutions, an integrated contract development and manufacturing organization), Complex Hospital Generics (Piramal Critical Care) and Piramal Consumer Healthcare (over-the-counter consumer and wellness products).
- Quality is presented as a core moat: "Best-in-Class Quality: Sellersville facility in the US received an Establishment Inspection Report from the US FDA, successfully concluding the inspection. Maintain our Zero OAI status till date."
- CHG leadership positions are stated as: "Maintained leadership in Sevoflurane, #1 Rank with 48% value share" in the US, and "Maintained #1 Rank in intrathecal Baclofen in the US" (source for all market-share data: IQVIA).
- CDMO demand backdrop framed as structurally favourable: "Biopharma funding in H1CY26 up over 100% vs H1CY25. (Industry reports)" and "Geopolitical & trade uncertainties are accelerating supply-chain diversification, driving demand for reliable multi-site CDMO partners."
- Chairperson Nandini Piramal guides to "delivering sustained revenue growth and EBITDA expansion through FY27, while staying agile amid a dynamic external environment."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Partnership] "Collaborated with Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services for next-gen conjugation technology" — site-specific conjugation for homogeneous, higher-quality ADCs that "Works on native antibodies — no antibody re-engineering", under a two-way referral plus technology transfer Master Technology Agreement.
- [Associate/JV] AbbVie Therapeutics India Pvt. Ltd., a JV between AbbVie and PPL, is described as "one of the market leaders in the Indian ophthalmology segment", with FY2026 revenue of ₹526 Cr and a 23% PAT margin; market-leading brands listed are Pred Forte (eye inflammation), Lumigan, Combigan and Alphagan (glaucoma) and Refresh Tears (dry eyes). The deck adds "PPL CDMO business supplies ophthalmology products to the JV".
- [Minority investment] "PPL has a strategic minority investment in Yapan Bio Private Limited, that operates in the biologics / bio-therapeutics and vaccine segments"; the facility count footnote states "Includes one facility via PPL's minority investment in Yapan Bio."
- [Regulatory/quality] Sellersville (US) received an EIR from the US FDA concluding the inspection; the CDMO business "continues to maintain its Zero OAI track record to date".
- [Exceptional item] Q1FY26 exceptional items "include one-time insolvency proceeds received from a claim filed against a third-party supplier of our complex hospital generics business, with the NCLT in November 2023"; there was no exceptional item in Q1FY27.

deepdive.thesis: Piramal Pharma is a vertically integrated CDMO with growing specialty generics and consumer healthcare segments, benefiting from global supply chain diversification and high-margin contract manufacturing. Its strategic partnerships and capacity expansion position it for sustained revenue growth despite margin pressures in generics.

open.item: Management expects to deliver broad-based revenue growth accompanied by margin expansion in FY2027.
The Complex Hospital Generics business is expected to deliver stronger performance in FY2027, supported by ramp-up of inhalation anesthesia sales outside the US and integration of Kenalog.
Management expects a gradual pickup in inhalation anesthesia growth in markets outside the US from FY2027 after competition-driven softness.
Investing US$90 Million to scale sterile injectable and payload linker capabilities at the Lexington and Riverview sites, with the Lexington expansion scheduled for completion by the end of CY2027.
Focus on premiumisation of the Consumer Healthcare portfolio by launching fewer but high-potential products with better success rates and a clear emphasis on high-margin products.
Continue focused initiatives with suppliers and partner networks to alleviate supply constraints in the Injectable Pain Management portfolio and improve product availability.
Remain aligned with the SBTi-approved decarbonisation roadmap with heightened emphasis on increasing renewable energy adoption across sites.
Management flags intensified competition in inhalation anesthesia across markets outside the US as a drag on growth.

Management flags dependence on biopharma funding cycles and on a key customer, after inventory destocking by a key customer for a leading on-patent commercial product and soft early-stage CDMO order inflows in H1.

risks.note: Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: the Company's ability to meet patient needs, create value and build trust is directly linked to the quality and safety of its products, and poor performance in these critical areas can have negative impacts on stakeholders and in turn on the business. Mitigation is a shift from 'Quality for Compliance' to 'Quality as a Culture' across systems, processes, technology and people, with a dedicated Corporate Quality Assurance Group monitoring adherence to defined product quality standards.

Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: PPL is subject to regulations related to bribery, corruption, lobbying and similar areas, and as standards keep changing any non-compliance may result in financial impact and harm to reputation. Mitigated through codes of conduct for board members, senior management, employees, suppliers, vendors and contractors across the value chain.
risks.risk: Business ethics — bribery, corruption and lobbying compliance

risks.note: Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: a data breach within the Company's IT systems can lead to serious business impact and reputational risk, resulting in both financial and non-financial losses, with regulations tightening and awareness rising. Mitigated by a privacy policy governing personal information and by Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) scans reported to IT and application teams.

Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: the Company must stay focused on the needs and wellbeing of patients, customers and consumers as regulations become stricter; addressed through its core principles of Knowledge, Action, Care and Impact and steps to improve engagement and outcomes, with patient centricity as a key priority.
risks.risk: Patient, customer and consumer centricity under tightening regulation

risks.note: Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR — exports contribute 72.78% of the entity's total turnover and markets served span over 100 countries, so earnings depend on overseas demand, regulatory regimes and currency movements rather than the domestic market.
100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — manufacturing of pharmaceuticals, medicinal, chemical and botanical products — leaving no diversification outside the pharmaceutical cycle.

The permanent-employee turnover rate was 23% in FY2026 (25.50% in FY2025 and 21.94% in FY2024), against a much lower permanent-worker turnover of 5%, indicating sustained churn in the professional workforce that supports a science- and quality-led business.

The Board reports a Risk Management framework to identify, measure, manage and mitigate business risks and opportunities, which helps manage market, credit and operational risks and quantifies potential impact at Company level; details of the risk management process sit in the MD&A.
risks.risk: Market, credit and operational risks managed through the enterprise risk framework
